{{Given name hatnote|Ramakrishnan|Alladi|lang=Malayali}}'''Alladi Ramakrishnan''' (9 August 1923 – 7 June 2008) was an Indian physicist and the founder of the [[Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai|Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] (IMSc) in [[Chennai]]. He made contributions to [[stochastic process]], [[particle physics]], algebra of [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrices]], [[special theory of relativity]] and [[quantum mechanics]].

== Early life ==
Ramakrishnan was born on 9 August 1923 in [[Madras]]. His father was the lawyer [[Sir Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer]], who, as a member of the Constituent Assembly, was instrumental in drafting the [[Constitution of India]] with other prominent members. He had his early education in P. S. High School, Madras. He graduated from [[Presidency College, Madras]], with [[B.Sc.|B.Sc. (Hons)]] degree in physics. As a student of the college he had wanted to work under [[Sir C. V. Raman]]. When his father consulted Raman, Raman suggested reading ''Lehrbuch der theoretischen Physik''<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=qFBivgAACAAJ Lehrbuch der theoretischen Physik], snippets from [[Google Books]]</ref> by [[Georg Joos]]. Ramakrishnan studied the book and developed an interest in [[theoretical physics]] and [[special relativity]] in particular.<ref>{{cite web|title=An interview with Professor Alladi Ramakrishnan|url=http://www.rediff.com/news/aug/18alladi.htm|publisher=Rediff On The NeT|access-date=18 August 2010}}</ref>

== Career ==
After completing his studies at Presidency College, Ramakrishnan started working with [[Homi J. Bhabha|Homi Bhabha]] at the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR). At TIFR, Bhabha introduced him to Cascade Theory and Fluctuation Problem of Cosmic Radiation. In August 1949, he left for England to work under [[M. S. Bartlett]] at the [[University of Manchester]]. Ramakrishnan's work on Product Densities that he did while at TIFR was good enough work for a PhD. But he stayed in Manchester for two more years to complete his residency requirements. His work on Product Densities appeared in the Proceedings of the [[Cambridge Philosophical Society]].<ref name="alladik"/>

During the 1950s, he worked on the problem of Fluctuating Density Field, and published a series of eight papers on the subject. During 1957–1958 Ramakrishnan visited the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton. It was the Institute of Advanced Study that inspired him to start a similar institution in India.<ref name="alladik"/> Ramakrishnan is noted for his work in quantum mechanics on giving a prescription for transition from [[Pauli matrices|Pauli]] to [[Dirac matrices]]. He also published several papers giving simple but insightful geometric derivations for the [[Lorentz transformations]].<ref name="alladik"/>

== Creation of Matscience ==
After his return to Madras (Chennai) from the Institute for Advanced Study in 1958, Ramakrishnan began a Theoretical Physics Seminar in his family home ''Ekamra Nivas'' (house with a mango tree). In the seminar he presented lectures on the latest advances in theoretical physics to a small group of students, and invited leading scientists from the world to address the students. In 1960, nobel laureate [[Niels Bohr]] visited India and was impressed by the small group of students trained by Ramakrishnan.<ref name="alladik">{{cite web|last=Alladi|first=Krishnaswami|title=Contributions of Professor Alladi Ramakrishnan to the Mathematical Sciences|url=http://krishnaswami-alladi.com/old-website/arcontributions.pdf|publisher=University of Florida|access-date=18 August 2010}}</ref> While in India, Bohr visited Dr. Ramakrishnan's family home, and inspired the creation of an institute for advanced research.<ref name="alladik"/><ref name="hin"/> With Bohr's recommendation and with support from the then prime minister of India, [[Jawaharlal Nehru]] and C.Subramaniam, Alladi Ramakrishan set out to create the institute. [[Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai|Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] (Matscience) was thus created in 1962 with Ramakrishnan as the director. [[Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar]], nobel laureate and professor at [[University of Chicago]] inaugurated the Institute at the [[Presidency College, Chennai|Presidency College]] in the then Madras. Chandrasekhar also agreed to be an Honorary Professor of Astrophysics at the institute and addressed its first students.<ref>{{cite news|last=Staff Reporter|title=Alladi Ramakrishnan, 85, Scientist, Passes Away|url=http://www.indiajournal.com/pages/event.php?id=3846|access-date=18 August 2010|newspaper=India Journal|date=13 Jul 2008}}{{Dead link|date=September 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Ramakrishnan travelled and lectured extensively during his years at Matscience, holding lectures at over 200 centers of learning. He was unusually generous with providing opportunity and leave for his Ph.D. students to travel to centers of learning abroad, firmly believing that this was of benefit to his students and that research was an international activity, even if this brought with it the risk of losing talented students to other institutions. After retiring, Ramakrishnan continued to teach and inspire. In the last decades of his life, several high school students and undergraduates came to his home in Madras to learn with him, subsequently pursuing higher studies in the United States towards a career of research.<ref name="alladik"/>

== Personal life and death ==
Ramakrishnan was married to Lalitha Ramakrishnan, the daughter of mathematics professor H. Subramani Iyer. His son [[Krishnaswami Alladi]] is  a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Florida]], [[Gainesville, Florida]].<ref name="alladik" /> Ramakrishnan was a connoisseur of [[Carnatic music]] and strongly believed that art and science can go hand in hand.<ref name="hin">{{cite news|title=Alladi Ramakrishnan passes away|url=http://www.hindu.com/2008/06/09/stories/2008060954341100.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080611051702/http://www.hindu.com/2008/06/09/stories/2008060954341100.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 June 2008|access-date=18 August 2010|location=Chennai, India|newspaper=[[The Hindu]]|date=9 June 2008}}</ref> He died on 7 June 2008 at his son's home in Gainesville, Florida.<ref>{{cite web|last=Alladi|first=Krishnaswami|title=Remembering my father Professor Alladi Ramakrishnan|url=http://krishnaswami-alladi.com//old-website/ark.html|access-date=18 August 2010}}</ref>
